text.en:
One morning there was no milk, no vegetable seller, the sweeper did not come and the bus did not run.
Nisha realised how much she depended on people she hardly noticed.
"Every kind of work matters," her mother said.

Work is what people do to earn a living or to take care of others. Farmers grow food, tailors stitch clothes, teachers teach, drivers carry people and doctors heal.
Some work is paid, such as a job or a business. Some work is unpaid but very important, such as cooking and caring for the family at home.
We depend on each other's work. No one can do everything for themselves. This is called interdependence.
All honest work deserves respect. The dignity of labour means that no honest work is small or low.
Work gives us money, skills, pride and a sense of purpose. We should also learn to share household work and respect those who work with their hands.
Work is what people do to earn a living or look after others.
Some work is paid and some is unpaid, like caring for family at home. Both are important.
We depend on each other's work. This is interdependence.
All honest work deserves respect. This is the dignity of labour.

problem.en: Is cooking at home work even if no one pays for it?

text.en: Cooking is useful and takes time and effort.
It is unpaid, but it keeps the family healthy.
So yes, it is real and important work.

prompt.en: A friend laughs at a child whose father sweeps the road. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Sweepers keep our city clean and healthy, so we depend on them.

points.en: Work earns a living or cares for others.
Paid and unpaid work both matter.
